cells.tense: Your hands are on the material now, and they are learning how it takes shape.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Take what you have been pushing toward an end. Call it finished enough, set it down, and keep only the unfinished part in your hands.
cells.core:
You steer by tending what is actually here — how it grows, what it needs, what shape it is taking. The direction is not a decision you made once and left standing; you read it off the work itself. That is why you can tell when something is done without anyone approving it. Care teaches you the finish line.

The hands that learn how something flourishes also learn when to stop feeding it. Take what you have been pushing toward an end. Call it finished enough, set it down, and keep only the unfinished part. It will not feel like losing if you let the work tell you. What is done gets laid down; what is not stays with you, and the direction stays clean because the finished thing is no longer muddying it.
cells.sheetLine: The work itself tells you when it is finished.
cells.verb: learning how things grow by tending them
cells.place: at the point where a direction gets chosen and held

cells.tense: You are already past the next harvest in your head, and the ground you have is standing empty.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Where you catch yourself fixing a result, picture the next step just once — then take it, and let what comes be whatever it is.
cells.core:
You are tending what does not exist yet. The plan for how it will flourish arrives before anything is in the ground, and your hands keep reaching toward a version that has not been given. Pushing that hard toward a result you cannot see keeps you working past the material — and the material is the only place you actually learn from, so it sits untouched.

Where you catch yourself fixing an outcome, picture the next step once. Not the whole design — the single step you would take if the result did not matter. Then take it, and let what comes of it be whatever it is. You will learn more from what actually happens than from what you braced for, and the next direction shows itself in the doing. One real step beats a season of planned harvest.

cells.tense: You stood at the door of choosing, and the door is still standing behind you.
cells.act: ask the beginner's question about where to go
cells.ask: Ask someone who does this well what they would try first. Ask as a beginner, with no position to hold, and walk toward whatever their answer opens.
cells.core:
You know what direction looks like when it has a body: hands on something, learning it by doing, keeping it alive because you keep feeding it. None of that has been lifted lately. What you once cultivated has no heat in it now.

Ask someone who does this well what they would try first. Ask as a beginner, with no position to hold, and walk toward whatever their answer opens. Do not push effort into the cold place; the spark is what pulls direction back. A question asked fresh does that work. You do not need to feel ready — you only need to be curious enough to ask, and the asking is already a little fire.

cells.tense: You are already steering — the course is set — and the hand on the wheel is not on the record.
cells.act: govern by knowing what to surrender
cells.ask: Name a decision you have been running without calling it yours, claim it plainly, and let go of one rule you set on how it has to turn out.
cells.core:
The direction is being set. Something got shaped by care, someone learned how the thing grows, and whoever did the shaping is not in the account. It gets described as the circumstances, or the people who needed it, or what anybody would have done. That is the disowning — the steering works and the hand is off the wheel.

So put the hand back on. Name a decision you have been running without calling it yours, and claim it plainly. Then let go of one rule you set on it — the one that says it has to come out a certain way or it does not count. Directing by what you can release is the older and simpler move. Begin there, and the course is yours again.
cells.sheetLine: The course is being steered, and your hand is not on the wheel.
cells.verb: learning how things grow by tending them
cells.place: at the point where a direction gets chosen and held
